subject: Literacy
title: What happens first?
objectives: Children will put three pictures of a story in order.
Children will use first, then and last with support.
content: Putting three pictures of a story in order, using first, then and last, and telling the story back.
teachingActivities: Use stories with clear everyday events such as getting dressed or planting a seed; place cards left to right as you speak; use the words first, then and last every time; accept actions and words.
learnerActivities: Put three pictures of a story in order and use first, then and last with support.
resources: Three-picture story sets: planting a seed, washing hands, going to sleep
A real seed, soil, a pot and water
assessment: Observe whether each child orders three pictures and uses at least one sequencing word.
expectedOutcomes: Uses at least one sequencing word.

lessons.title: Planting a seed
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will put three pictures of planting a seed in order.
successCriteria: Puts three pictures in order with support
Names what happens in each picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can retell a short story with props, use words such as first, then and the end, and follow two-step instructions.
resources: Three picture cards: digging, planting a seed, watering
A pot, soil and a seed
lessons.starter: Show the pot, soil and seed and say "First we put soil in the pot. Then we plant the seed. Then we water it."
teacherActivities: Show the three picture cards in the right order and say first, then, last.
Mix the cards and ask "What happens first?"
Do the activity: put soil in the pot, plant a seed and water it.
Let the children put the cards in order.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the words.
Child points to the digging card.
Child puts cards in order with support.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the three picture cards in the right order and say first, then, last. Children: Children look and say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Mix the cards and ask "What happens first?" Children: Child points to the digging card.
Step 3. Teacher: Do the activity: put soil in the pot, plant a seed and water it. Children: Children help with each step.
Step 4. Teacher: Let the children put the cards in order. Children: Child puts cards in order with support.

practical.title: Plant a seed
steps: Plant a seed and water it.
Put the three picture cards in order.
practical.safety: Use clean soil and wash hands after. Do not let children eat soil or seeds. Supervise water and wipe spills.

differentiation.support: Hold the cards together and place them in order.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what happens first, then and last.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What happens first?
questions.expected: We put soil in the pot.

expectedOutcomes: Uses first and last with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the pot in a sunny place and say "We will watch it grow."
lessons.homeConnection: Plant a seed with your child at home and talk about what happens first.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put three pictures of planting a seed in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Washing hands
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will put the steps of washing hands in order.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can retell a short story with props, use words such as first, then and the end, and follow two-step instructions.
resources: Three picture cards: wet hands, soap, dry hands
A basin, soap and a towel
lessons.starter: Say "First we wet our hands, then we use soap, last we dry them." Show the basin.
teacherActivities: Show the three cards in order and say first, then, last.
Mix the cards and ask the children to order them.
Wash hands together and say each step as you do it.
Ask "What did we do first?" and "What did we do last?"
learnerActivities: Children put the cards in order.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the three cards in order and say first, then, last. Children: Children say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Mix the cards and ask the children to order them. Children: Children put the cards in order.
Step 3. Teacher: Wash hands together and say each step as you do it. Children: Children wash hands in order.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What did we do first?" and "What did we do last?" Children: Child points to the cards.

practical.title: Wash and order
steps: Set up a basin with soap and a towel.
Wash hands in the right order.
Put the cards in order afterwards.
practical.safety: Use mild soap and a shallow basin. Supervise closely, wipe spills and make sure each child has a clean towel.

differentiation.support: Do the steps together and name each one.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend how to wash hands.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Orders the steps of washing hands
lessons.conclusion: Dry hands and say "First, then, last."
lessons.homeConnection: Say first, then, last when washing hands at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put the steps of washing hands in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Going to sleep
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will put three pictures about going to sleep in order.
successCriteria: Tells what happens in each picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can retell a short story with props, use words such as first, then and the end, and follow two-step instructions.
resources: Three picture cards: putting on pyjamas, a story, sleeping
lessons.starter: Hold the teddy and say "Teddy is tired. First pyjamas, then a story, last sleep."
teacherActivities: Show the three cards in order and say first, then, last.
Mix the cards and ask "What does Teddy do first?"
Act out the story with Teddy and the blanket.
Let each child place the cards in order.
learnerActivities: Child points to the pyjamas card.
Children pretend to put on pyjamas and sleep.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the three cards in order and say first, then, last. Children: Children say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Mix the cards and ask "What does Teddy do first?" Children: Child points to the pyjamas card.
Step 3. Teacher: Act out the story with Teddy and the blanket. Children: Children pretend to put on pyjamas and sleep.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child place the cards in order. Children: Child orders the cards.

practical.title: Teddy’s bedtime
steps: Put three cards on the mat.
Act out putting Teddy to bed.
practical.safety: Keep the area calm and use a clean blanket. Supervise sharing of the teddy.

differentiation.support: Act out the steps together and name them.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell their own bedtime steps.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Tuck Teddy in and whisper goodnight.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about your child’s bedtime steps using first, then and last.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put three pictures about going to sleep in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Telling the story back
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will tell a three-picture story back using first, then and last.
successCriteria: Uses at least one sequencing word
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can retell a short story with props, use words such as first, then and the end, and follow two-step instructions.
lessons.starter: Show a set of three cards and say "Who can tell what happens?"
teacherActivities: Choose a set and put the cards in order together.
Ask "What happens first?" and wait for the child to say it.
Ask "What happens next?" and "What happens last?"
Let each child tell the story with a puppet.
learnerActivities: Child puts cards in order with support.
Child tells the story to the group.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Choose a set and put the cards in order together. Children: Child puts cards in order with support.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What happens first?" and wait for the child to say it. Children: Child tells the first event.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What happens next?" and "What happens last?" Children: Child tells the next events.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child tell the story with a puppet. Children: Child tells the story to the group.

practical.title: Story telling
steps: Put three cards in order on the floor.
practical.safety: Never make a child talk if they do not want to. Accept words, actions or pointing.

differentiation.support: Point to each card and offer the first word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the story without looking at the cards.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Tells a three-part story in order
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to tell you what happened at school using first, then and last.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "tell a three-picture story back using first, then and last" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 order check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child orders and tells a short story.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can retell a short story with props, use words such as first, then and the end, and follow two-step instructions.
lessons.starter: Say "First, then, last" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: planting, washing and bedtime.
At each station ask the child to order the cards and tell the story.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: planting, washing and bedtime. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask the child to order the cards and tell the story. Children: Child orders and tells.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Story stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large soft cards.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a four-picture story.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: orders three pictures; uses first, then or last; tells the story back.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.homeConnection: Tell stories at home using first, then and last.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child orders and tells a short story" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
